scope: Phase 8 implementation and directly verified regressions; overall Casdoor equivalence remains incomplete.

flat_route_declarations.meaning: Static declaration coverage only; not functional completion.

syncers: Correct actual SQL columns and FromRow labels; shared validated REST/compatibility CRUD and masked credential preservation.
Real independent PostgreSQL source and LDAP bind/search imports, stable source-to-user links, explicit credential mapping and batch rollback.
Shared PostgreSQL due times, short leases, stale-worker fencing, bounded execution, failure backoff and disabled organization checks.
commerce: Durable original checkout request and provider credential fingerprint before remote I/O, cross-instance leases and bounded same-key retries after lost responses.
Authenticated Stripe status lookup and remote session expiry before stock release; PayPal approval-to-capture with persistent idempotency key and exact amount/currency validation.
Normal reconcile-order and REST order reconcile operations; API/Store driven rather than a background automatic scanner.
Immutable buyer UUID for every new order; ignore forged buyer fields, preserve renamed account ownership and reject reused-name takeover. Historical backfill uses explicit identity evidence only.
Current-name, qualified-name and UUID compatibility purchase queries resolve to the stored buyer identity. Ambiguous standalone legacy payment names are excluded from ordinary-user lists.
user_import: Real multipart XLSX first sheet plus JSON, CSV and TSV, bounded ZIP/XML/row/column parsing and atomic batch import.
Real current administrator and tenant checks, same-tenant LDAP references, preserved legacy IDs and no implicit MFA enrollment loss.
Casdoor password/type/salt semantics, independent compatibility vectors, masked import rejection and masked legacy update preservation.
Bounded KDF verification and compare-and-set legacy hash upgrades only after successful real password authentication.
frontend: User store with safe tenant catalog, plan period/pricing, coupon and recharge inputs, current wallet, own purchases/subscriptions, explicit payment continuation, reconcile and cancel.
Payment provider secrets omitted from catalog; wallet display preserves legacy currency fallback.
Syncer form sends canonical user and typed database/SSL/mapping configuration; desktop and 390px store rendering inspected.

validation.fresh_migrations: 001-035 applied successfully to independent final backend and browser databases.
validation.execution_count_note: lib and main each execute the same 38 unit tests; execution count is not a count of independent business scenarios.

frontend.provider_note: Browser recharge uses the development gateway plus authorized administrator settlement. Stripe/PayPal use real local HTTP protocol fixtures; production financial providers were not exercised.

deployment: Stop old writers and back up before migrations 033-035; do not mix old checkout/syncer implementations with the new schema.
Review orders with NULL buyer_id before enabling end-user operations. Migration does not infer identity from a currently reused name.
Provider credential changes or retries past the conservative idempotency deadline require reconciliation rather than blind recreation.
Share PostgreSQL and deployment configuration across instances; external sources require explicitly configured source credentials.
remaining: Paid refunds with corresponding subscription/role/balance reversal, reliable PayPal order void, actual auto-renew scheduling, cart and background automatic payment reconciliation.
Three-decimal currency accounting and multi-currency wallets.
Syncer external writeback, source deletion-to-local disable, affiliation-table lookup and values conversion; unsupported conversion is explicitly rejected and writeback absence is reported.
Imported MFA enrollment migration and complete dedicated import/export UI.
Real Kerberos ticket verification, broader SAML interoperability, Agent execution, OpenClaw/OTLP breadth, Marketplace themes and additional cloud providers.
Production gateway/directory/mail/SMS/cloud, hardware and cluster acceptance; 299/299 routes do not prove these capabilities.
